profile.reading:
The Pittock Internet Exchange occupies the Pittock Block building at 921 SW Washington Street in downtown Portland, Oregon, a historic structure originally built to house an electric substation and later converted into one of the Pacific Northwest's two primary carrier hotels and internet exchange points. On January 6, 2021, the building was acquired for a reported $326 million by Harrison Street and the 1547 Data Center Real Estate Fund II, an affiliate of fifteenfortyseven Critical Systems Realty ("1547"), in the second joint acquisition between the two firms following their earlier purchase of the Wells Building in Milwaukee. The operator listed for this record, Alco Properties, is the building's prior owner and is no longer the operator of record; Alco's own web domain, pittock.com, currently redirects to an unrelated third-party blog rather than any data center or property-management content, and no current Alco Properties web presence describing this facility was located.

Under 1547, the 302,200-square-foot building operates as facility "PTOR1," serving 179 service providers at the time of acquisition and offering direct access to seven subsea telecommunications cables, positioning it among the most connected buildings in the country and roughly 18 miles from Intel's Hillsboro headquarters, in one of the fastest-growing data center submarkets in the world. In February 2023, 1547 announced an expanded partnership with the network operator Arelion to add 400G-capable connectivity, global 40G Ethernet virtual-circuit enablement, and direct regional links to Arelion's Hillsboro point of presence, alongside access to AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Oracle, and IBM Cloud. That same upgrade program added N+1 (Tier III-equivalent) generation, UPS, and chiller capacity, and a new utility vault initially sized at 3.6 megawatts with room to expand to 8.5 megawatts; the first phase added roughly 20,000 square feet of new white space and 2 megawatts of capacity on the building's fourth floor.

The building's role as the region's meet-me-room and internet exchange point, historically known as NWAX, the Northwest Access Exchange, is its defining public identity: this is fundamentally carrier and network infrastructure rather than a cloud or enterprise data hall, and its value comes from interconnection density rather than raw compute capacity. Beyond the disclosed vault and phase-one figures above, 1547 has not published a full building-wide power or capacity specification, consistent with how most operating colocation providers disclose incrementally as they market new space rather than all at once.

"Alco Properties" is a stale operator tag; Alco Properties is no longer the operator of record and publishes no current facility specs.

reading.body:
The Pittock Internet Exchange is an internet peering facility, not a data center, housed in a 1913 historic building occupying a city block in downtown Portland. It hosts a NWAX point of presence serving as Portland's internet exchange point. No power consumption, rack count, or IT capacity is published for this facility.

The facility publishes no megawatt specification and therefore ranks outside the eight Oregon data center campuses with published power figures. Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities total and 156.6 MW of published IT load capacity across all operators. Without published power data, this campus's actual role in Oregon's infrastructure cannot be assessed from the specifications alone.

The operator's web presence could not be located and the facility's published domain resolves to an unrelated page. The facility identity was confirmed through independent sources as a historic building housing an internet exchange, but current operator contact information and any capacity specifications are not available on the operator's published channels.
